title: ACTORS FROM THE LONDON STAGE PRESENTS MUCH ADO ABOUT NOTHING
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Presenting Series Exuberant, joyful, and above all, ravishingly entertaining, Much Ado About Nothing is one of Shakespeare's most celebrated and enduringly popular comedies. This delightful romp deftly explores notions of identity, marriage, and communication through the sparring between Benedick and Beatrice, two of Shakespeare's most gloriously realized characters. With its piquant blend of prickly banter, mistaken identities, and swoon-worthy romance, Much Ado About Nothing is sheer theatrical delight. Much Ado About Nothing is brought to life by Actors From The London Stage, the renowned 5-actor touring group founded in 1975 by Dr. Homer "Murph" Swander and Sir Patrick Stewart, along with many other celebrated actors from the Royal Shakespeare Company. This remarkable company has called Shakespeare at Notre Dame its artistic home since 2000, and travels to multiple colleges and universities nationwide twice annually. Each member of this self-directed ensemble assumes multiple roles while favoring minimal props and costumes, creating a theatrical experience unlike any other. ASL available for Friday's performance. For tickets within view of the ASL interpreter, click here. Co-sponsored by Shakespeare at Notre Dame.

title: BEN SCHMIDT-SWARTZ QUARTET
location: Merrimans’ Playhouse | 401 E. Colfax Ave., Suite 135 | South Bend, IN 46617
description:
The Ben Schmidt-Swartz Quartet explores original music as well as some choice jazz standards that are meaningful to the band and fun to play. The aesthetic comes out of a tradition of decades of reference points from the great saxophone quartets from jazz history. From Coleman Hawkins, to John Coltrane; from Lester Young and Oscar Peterson to Dexter Gordon, this group hopes to honor, and continue in that legacy.

Ben Schmidt-Swartz - saxophone

Matthew Fries - piano

Carlo De Rosa - bass

Nelson Oliva - drums

title: CHICKEN RUN (2000)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Browning Cinema Professor Pfinklepfunder's $1 Sunday Films Directed by Peter Lord, Nick Park With Phil Daniels, Lynn Ferguson, Tony Haygarth Rated G, 84 minutes, Blu-ray The plasticine adventures of Wallace & Gromit are well known around the globe and have garnered shelfloads of awards. Roughly 25 years ago, the creative team behind that expansive world forged a new creative path using the same stop-motion animation style but with a new set of characters in Chicken Run. Borrowing from Steve McQueen's The Great Escape, Chicken Run is also a breakout adventure, but with the likes of chickens who live on an egg farm that certainly looks more like a prisoner-of-war camp and not a cage-free shady acres. A rebel in the henhouse, Ginger, incites upheaval as she leads her fellow feathered friends on a mission to free and save their lives. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

title: EXHIBITION OPENING | MELI BANDERA: “GENERATION GAPS: ODES TO FAMILIAL MEMORIES.”
location: IU South Bend Civil Rights Heritage Center | 1040 W. Washington | South Bend, IN 46601
description:
Meli Bandera (they/them) crafts soft altars built from paper, felt, and wool to capture the memories of those who came before them: the scent of their grandmother’s garden after she waters it, the rhythmic thump of a lawnmower on a summer afternoon, or the shared sweetness of bolis enjoyed with loved ones. Bandera builds these memories into tangible forms, acknowledging the gaps and absences that shape our understanding of family history.

Bandera’s fiber-based artworks are devotional gestures, mirroring the way memories shift and transform over time. Imagine a watermelon lemonade that will never be made by an abuela again, or a bisabuela walking to the centro for water. These are the threads Bandera pulls from, using recycled pulp, cochineal dye, and wool to create pieces that feel both ancient and present. These works are a form of time travel, using softness and humor to stretch grief and joy across eras.

“Generation Gaps” opens with an evening event at the Civil Rights Heritage Center on Thursday, September 10, 2026, from 6:00 – 7:30 PM. Light refreshments will be served as you experience Bandera’s deeply moving work. The exhibit remains on view through December 10 during the Center's public hours.

Details at crhc.iusb.edu.

title: GREY GARDENS (1975)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Browning Cinema Sunday Docs Directed by Ellen Hovde, Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Muffie Meyer With Little Edie Bouvier Beale, Edith Bouvier Beale, Brooks Hyers Rated PG, 94 minutes, DCP Meet Big and Little Edie Beale: mother and daughter, high-society dropouts, and reclusive cousins of Jackie Onassis. The two manage to thrive together (with the help of some raccoons) amid the decay and disorder of their East Hampton, New York, mansion, making for an eerily ramshackle echo of the American Camelot. An impossibly intimate portrait, this 1976 documentary by Albert and David Maysles, codirected by Ellen Hovde and Muffie Meyer, quickly became a cult classic and established Little Edie as a fashion icon and philosopher queen. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Documentary Film.

title: LA DIVINA COMETA (2022)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Browning Cinema New at the Browning Directed by Mimmo Paladino Not Rated, 93 minutes, DCP In Italian with English subtitles Discussion scheduled to follow screening! A journey through a vast fresco painted with light. Its characters come together like figures in a Nativity scene, weaving stories, symbols, and words between folk tradition and experimental exploration. Dante, a silent witness, passes through it alongside Ugolino and Pontormo, Glenn Gould and Giordano Bruno. A poor family searches for shelter while awaiting five wandering Magi bearing gifts of music, theatre, painting, poetry—and nothingness. Will the Divine Comet lead them forth to see the stars again? This film is being screened as part of the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art's temporary exhibition Mimmo Paladino: Present into Past. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Joseph Becherer, exhibition curator and director of the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art, and Theodore J. Cachey Jr., Pizzo Family Chair in Dante Studies. This is a free but ticketed event. To guarantee your seat, please pick up your tickets at least 15 minutes prior to the show, at which point your unclaimed tickets may be used to seat patrons waiting on standby. Tickets will be available for pick-up at the Ticket Office beginning one hour prior to the performance. Co-sponsored by the Raclin Murphy Museum of Art, Italian Studies Center.
